Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

History[edit]

 Desktop version
  • Desktop 1.4.5.0:
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons.
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.
  • Desktop 1.4.4:
    • Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. This includes such weapons as Dart Guns, Flamethrowers, and Star Cannons. This category of weapons is being referred to as "specialist" weapons.
    • Fixed a tooltip display bug that caused any weapons buffed by Shroomite headpieces to display their damage 1 higher than it should have been.
  • Desktop 1.4.0.1:
    • Sprites updated.
    • Shroomite Breastplate now properly displays +13% ranged damage in its tooltip.
  • Desktop 1.2.2: Increased the ranged damage bonus in stealth mode from 50% to 60% and the aggro reduction from 600 to 750.
  • Desktop 1.2.1.2:
    • Flame and Frozen Wings now fade when stealthed.
    • Some enemies will no longer chase players depending on level of stealth and distance.
    • Shroomite armor no longer loses stealth when using items.
  • Desktop 1.2.1: Updated female sprite.
  • Desktop 1.2: Introduced.

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop, Console, and Mobile versions of Terraria.
For the differences of this information on Old-gen console and 3DS, see Legacy:Shroomite armor.
Shroomite armor
Statistics
Type
ArmorSet
Defense51 (set)
Set BonusNot moving puts you in stealth,
increasing ranged ability and reducing chance for enemies to target you
Rarity08*
Sell18 GC (set)

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

History[edit]

 Desktop version
  • Desktop 1.4.5.0:
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons.
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.
  • Desktop 1.4.4:
    • Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. This includes such weapons as Dart Guns, Flamethrowers, and Star Cannons. This category of weapons is being referred to as "specialist" weapons.
    • Fixed a tooltip display bug that caused any weapons buffed by Shroomite headpieces to display their damage 1 higher than it should have been.
  • Desktop 1.4.0.1:
    • Sprites updated.
    • Shroomite Breastplate now properly displays +13% ranged damage in its tooltip.
  • Desktop 1.2.2: Increased the ranged damage bonus in stealth mode from 50% to 60% and the aggro reduction from 600 to 750.
  • Desktop 1.2.1.2:
    • Flame and Frozen Wings now fade when stealthed.
    • Some enemies will no longer chase players depending on level of stealth and distance.
    • Shroomite armor no longer loses stealth when using items.

It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0. * The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied ''after'' applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, [[accessories]], and [[buffs]]. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their [[tooltips]] would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a [[Ranger Emblem]] would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%. * The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the [[Psycho Knife]]. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority. ** The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.GetWeaponKnockback}} * [[NPCs]] will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show [[emotes]] to) players that are in stealth mode.{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|property=Terraria.Player.CanBeTalkedTo}} * Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes {{duration|5 ticks}} before the process resumes. * Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.Update}} For instance, when moving at a steady {{mph|2 pixels}}, it takes {{duration|floor(1/(0.0075*2)) ticks}} to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes {{duration|floor(1/(0.0075*10)) ticks}} when moving at {{mph|10 pixels}}. * Using the [[Rod of Discord]], [[Hook of Dissonance]], or [[Rod of Harmony]] will not cancel stealth mode. == Tips == * This armor set has good synergy with the [[Sniper Rifle]], as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of [[ammo conservation]], and also adds an additional +25% summon damage. * The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For [[PvP]] purposes, consider using the [[Familiar set]] in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible [[accessories]]. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players. ** Using an [[Invisibility Potion]] can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice. * Some [[dye]] combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at [[night]]: File:Shroomite armor with Black Dye.png|[[Black Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Blue and Silver Dye.png|[[Blue and Silver Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Frost armor and Red Dye.png|Left: [[Frost armor]] and without dye; right: [[Red Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Red and Black Dye.png|[[Red and Black Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Red and Black Dye at night.png|Red and Black Dye at night == Trivia == * Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense. * Wearing a Shroomite Mask with [[Silver Dye]] can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull. == History == {{history|Desktop 1.4.5.0| ** Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons. ** Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.}} {{history|Desktop 1.4.4| ** Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop, Console, and Mobile versions of Terraria.
For the differences of this information on Old-gen console and 3DS, see Legacy:Shroomite armor.
Shroomite armor
Statistics
Type
ArmorSet
Defense51 (set)
Set BonusNot moving puts you in stealth,
increasing ranged ability and reducing chance for enemies to target you
Rarity08*
Sell18 GC (set)

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

History[edit]

 Desktop version
  • Desktop 1.4.5.0:
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons.
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.
  • Desktop 1.4.4:
    • Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. This includes such weapons as Dart Guns, Flamethrowers, and Star Cannons. This category of weapons is being referred to as "specialist" weapons.
    • Fixed a tooltip display bug that caused any weapons buffed by Shroomite headpieces to display their damage 1 higher than it should have been.
  • Desktop 1.4.0.1:
    • Sprites updated.
    • Shroomite Breastplate now properly displays +13% ranged damage in its tooltip.
  • Desktop 1.2.2: Increased the ranged damage bonus in stealth mode from 50% to 60% and the aggro reduction from 600 to 750.
  • Desktop 1.2.1.2:
    • Flame and Frozen Wings now fade when stealthed.
    • Some enemies will no longer chase players depending on level of stealth and distance.

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop, Console, and Mobile versions of Terraria.
For the differences of this information on Old-gen console and 3DS, see Legacy:Shroomite armor.
Shroomite armor
Statistics
Type
ArmorSet
Defense51 (set)
Set BonusNot moving puts you in stealth,
increasing ranged ability and reducing chance for enemies to target you
Rarity08*
Sell18 GC (set)

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

History[edit]

 Desktop version
  • Desktop 1.4.5.0:
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons.
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.
  • Desktop 1.4.4:
    • Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. This includes such weapons as Dart Guns, Flamethrowers, and Star Cannons. This category of weapons is being referred to as "specialist" weapons.
    • Fixed a tooltip display bug that caused any weapons buffed by Shroomite headpieces to display their damage 1 higher than it should have been.
  • Desktop 1.4.0.1:
    • Sprites updated.

  • Desktop 1.2.2: Increased the ranged damage bonus in stealth mode from 50% to 60% and the aggro reduction from 600 to 750.
  • Desktop 1.2.1.2:
    • Flame and Frozen Wings now fade when stealthed.
    • Some enemies will no longer chase players depending on level of stealth and distance.

{"apiUrl":"https://terraria.wiki.gg/api.php","requestedPageTitle":"Shroomite Leggings","pageTitle":"Shroomite armor","pageId":4771,"revisionTimestamp":"2026-05-22T12:53:49Z","fetchedAt":"2026-06-03T13:07:03.740Z","wikitext":"{{legacy nav tab}} {{item infobox | imagebreak = yes | type = Armor/Set | hardmode = yes }} '''Shroomite armor''' is a [[Hardmode]], post-[[Plantera]] ranged [[armor]] set consisting of the '''Shroomite Breastplate''' and '''Shroomite Leggings''', as well as three different headpieces: the '''Shroomite Headgear''', '''Shroomite Mask''', and '''Shroomite Helmet''', providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of [[ammunition]]. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 [[Shroomite Bar]]s (810 [[Glowing Mushroom]]s and 270 [[Chlorophyte Ore]]). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: |-|With Headgear= * +{{getSetInfo|Shroomite armor|defense|note=n}} [[defense]] * +13% [[ranged damage]] * ×1.12 damage of [[bows]], [[repeaters]], [[arrows]], and [[Stake]]s |-|With Mask= * +{{getSetInfo|Shroomite armor|defense|note=n}} [[defense]] * +13% [[ranged damage]] * ×1.12 damage of [[guns]], [[bullets]], and [[Candy Corn]] |-|With Helmet= * +{{getSetInfo|Shroomite armor|defense|note=n}} [[defense]] * +13% [[ranged damage]] * ×1.12 damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition * +25% ranged [[critical strike chance]] * +20% [[ammo conservation]] * +12% [[movement speed]] * The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving * Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter [[stealth]], which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents [[Fighter AI]] and [[Flying AI]] enemies from firing [[projectiles]] at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of {{duration|ceil(1/0.015) ticks}}, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.Update / Terraria.Player.GetWeaponKnockback}} ** +60% ranged damage ** +10% ranged critical strike chance ** −750 [[aggro]] ** +50% ranged [[knockback]] Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a [[Mounts|mount]]{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.Update}} or taking damage{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.Hurt}}. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (''see [[#Notes|Notes]] for details''). As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items ''(see [[Aggro#Target chasing|Aggro § Target chasing]] for details)''. == Set == {{infobox wrapper|direction=row|float=left |{{item infobox | hardmode = yes | auto = 1549 }} |{{item infobox | hardmode = yes | auto = 1550 }} }} {{-}} === Helmet variations === {{infobox wrapper|direction=row|float=left |{{item infobox | hardmode = yes | auto = 1546 }} |{{item infobox | hardmode = yes | auto = 1547 }} |{{item infobox | hardmode = yes | auto = 1548 }} }} {{-}} == Crafting == === Recipes === {{recipes|cate=force|link=no|result=Shroomite Breastplate/Shroomite Leggings/Shroomite Headgear/Shroomite Helmet/Shroomite Mask|expectedrows=5}} == Notes == [[File:Invisible Player.png|thumb|A player in stealth mode revealed by a [[Wisp in a Bottle|Wisp]].]] * The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. [[launchers]], the [[Star Cannon]], [[Flamethrower]], [[Dart Rifle]], etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the [[Harpoon]], [[Paintball Gun]], [[Toxikarp]], and [[Piranha Gun]]).{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.GetWeaponDamage}} ** The only exception is the [[Coin Gun]]. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0. * The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied ''after'' applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, [[accessories]], and [[buffs]]. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their [[tooltips]] would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a [[Ranger Emblem]] would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%. * The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the [[Psycho Knife]]. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority. ** The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.GetWeaponKnockback}} * [[NPCs]] will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show [[emotes]] to) players that are in stealth mode.{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|property=Terraria.Player.CanBeTalkedTo}} * Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes {{duration|5 ticks}} before the process resumes. * Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.{{source code ref|v=1.4.4.9|method=Terraria.Player.Update}} For instance, when moving at a steady {{mph|2 pixels}}, it takes {{duration|floor(1/(0.0075*2)) ticks}} to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes {{duration|floor(1/(0.0075*10)) ticks}} when moving at {{mph|10 pixels}}. * Using the [[Rod of Discord]], [[Hook of Dissonance]], or [[Rod of Harmony]] will not cancel stealth mode. == Tips == * This armor set has good synergy with the [[Sniper Rifle]], as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit. * Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine. * If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for [[Red Riding Leggings]] will both increase ranged {{DPS}} and also increase [[Summon weapons|summon damage]] if using the Red Riding Leggings. ** Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the [[Red Riding Dress]] will provide greater {{DPS}}, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of [[ammo conservation]], and also adds an additional +25% summon damage. * The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For [[PvP]] purposes, consider using the [[Familiar set]] in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible [[accessories]]. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players. ** Using an [[Invisibility Potion]] can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice. * Some [[dye]] combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at [[night]]: File:Shroomite armor with Black Dye.png|[[Black Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Blue and Silver Dye.png|[[Blue and Silver Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Frost armor and Red Dye.png|Left: [[Frost armor]] and without dye; right: [[Red Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Red and Black Dye.png|[[Red and Black Dye]] File:Shroomite armor with Red and Black Dye at night.png|Red and Black Dye at night == Trivia == * Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense. * Wearing a Shroomite Mask with [[Silver Dye]] can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull. == History == {{history|Desktop 1.4.5.0| ** Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons. ** Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.}} {{history|Desktop 1.4.4| ** Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. This includes such weapons as Dart Guns, Flamethrowers, and Star Cannons. This category of weapons is being referred to as "specialist" weapons. ** Fixed a tooltip display bug that caused any weapons buffed by Shroomite headpieces to display their damage 1 higher than it should have been.}} {{history|Desktop 1.4.0.1| ** Sprites updated. ** Shroomite Breastplate now properly displays +13% ranged damage in its tooltip.}} {{history|Desktop 1.2.2|Increased the ranged damage bonus in stealth mode from 50% to 60% and the aggro reduction from 600 to 750.}} {{history|Desktop 1.2.1.2| ** Flame and Frozen Wings now fade when stealthed. ** Some enemies will no longer chase players depending on level of stealth and distance. ** Shroomite armor no longer loses stealth when using items.}} {{history|Desktop 1.2.1|Updated female sprite.}} {{history|Desktop 1.2|Introduced.}} {{history|Console 1.02|Introduced.}} {{history|Switch 1.0.711.6|Introduced.}} {{history|Mobile 1.2.6508|Introduced.}} {{history|3DS-Release|Introduced.}} == References == {{reflist|refs= This is not a typo. Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop, Console, and Mobile versions of Terraria.
For the differences of this information on Old-gen console and 3DS, see Legacy:Shroomite armor.
Shroomite armor
Statistics
Type
ArmorSet
Defense51 (set)
Set BonusNot moving puts you in stealth,
increasing ranged ability and reducing chance for enemies to target you
Rarity08*
Sell18 GC (set)

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).

Notes[edit]

A player in stealth mode revealed by a Wisp.
  • The Shroomite Helmet boosts all non-consumable ranged weapons that use neither arrows/Stakes nor bullets/Candy Corn as ammunition (e.g. launchers, the Star Cannon, Flamethrower, Dart Rifle, etc.), or no ammunition at all (e.g. the Harpoon, Paintball Gun, Toxikarp, and Piranha Gun).[5]
    • The only exception is the Coin Gun. It cannot receive a damage bonus due to its damage stat of 0.
  • The ×1.12 damage boost to the specific ammunition type is applied after applying damage increases from the rest of the armor set, accessories, and buffs. As a result, Shroomite headpieces provide a larger damage bonus than their tooltips would suggest. The overall effect is a ×1.12 increase to the potency of ranged damage bonuses (not counting the headpiece itself). For example, a Ranger Emblem would effectively increase ranged damage by 16.8% instead of 15%.
  • The Shroomite armor's stealth mode cannot be stacked with that of the Psycho Knife. If both items are used, the player can only receive stat changes from the Psycho Knife's stealth mode as it has the highest priority.
    • The only exception is the knockback bonus, which is always granted as long as the player is in stealth mode. For example, when using the Psycho Knife with the Shroomite armor, the player will gain +100% melee knockback and +50% ranged knockback at the same time when in stealth mode. However, this has little use in actual combat.[6]
  • NPCs will not attempt to "talk" to (i.e. show emotes to) players that are in stealth mode.[7]
  • Using an item pauses the process of entering stealth mode but does not reset it. Once the use animation of the item is finished, it takes 0.08 seconds before the process resumes.
  • Stealth mode fades quickly once the player starts moving, depending on the player's movement speed.[8] For instance, when moving at a steady 10 mph, it takes 1.1 seconds to fully exit stealth mode, whereas it only takes 0.22 seconds when moving at 51 mph.
  • Using the Rod of Discord, Hook of Dissonance, or Rod of Harmony will not cancel stealth mode.

Tips[edit]

  • This armor set has good synergy with the Sniper Rifle, as stealth massively boosts the Sniper Rifle's main strengths – damage and critical strike chance – even further. With the right loadout, each rifle shot can deal over 1000 damage, killing most non-boss enemies in one hit.
  • Since the stealth mode is canceled upon taking damage, and the player must stop attacking to regain stealth, the bonus is useless when facetanking or using an invulnerability machine.
  • If not using the stealth properties of this armor, swapping out the Shroomite Leggings for Red Riding Leggings will both increase ranged DPS and also increase summon damage if using the Red Riding Leggings.
    • Similarly, if using Shroomite headpieces, swapping out the Shroomite Breastplate for the Red Riding Dress will provide greater DPS, due to its +25% ranged damage compared to the Shroomite Breastplate's respective +13%, which will provide a larger number to increase multiplicatively. Furthermore, the Red Riding Dress retains the same amount of ammo conservation, and also adds an additional +25% summon damage.
  • The set does not truly make the player invisible, as the armor glows a deep blue. For PvP purposes, consider using the Familiar set in conjunction with Shroomite armor, and with no visible accessories. With stealth active, this can render the player completely invisible to other players.
    • Using an Invisibility Potion can be a viable alternative, but the buff will wear off immediately if the player is damaged in any way, making Shroomite armor a more consistent choice.
  • Some dye combinations make the character sprite appear near-invisible at night:
  • Black Dye
  • Blue and Silver Dye
  • Left: Frost armor and without dye; right: Red Dye
  • Red and Black Dye
  • Red and Black Dye at night

Trivia[edit]

  • Shroomite armor is the only set whose headpiece variants all grant the same amount of defense.
  • Wearing a Shroomite Mask with Silver Dye can make the player's head resemble a cracked skull.

History[edit]

 Desktop version
  • Desktop 1.4.5.0:
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear now applies its damage bonus to ammo as well as weapons.
    • Each piece of Shroomite headgear damage bonus has been reduced from 15% to 12%.
  • Desktop 1.4.4:
    • Shroomite Helmet now also applies its bonus to any ranged projectile shooting weapon which is not otherwise included by the gun or bow helmets. This includes such weapons as Dart Guns, Flamethrowers, and Star Cannons. This category of weapons is being referred to as "specialist" weapons.
    • Fixed a tooltip display bug that caused any weapons buffed by Shroomite headpieces to display their damage 1 higher than it should have been.
  • Desktop 1.4.0.1:
    • Sprites updated.
    • Shroomite Breastplate now properly displays +13% ranged damage in its tooltip.
  • Desktop 1.2.2: Increased the ranged damage bonus in stealth mode from 50% to 60% and the aggro reduction from 600 to 750.
  • Desktop 1.2.1.2:
    • Flame and Frozen Wings now fade when stealthed.
    • Some enemies will no longer chase players depending on level of stealth and distance.
    • Shroomite armor no longer loses stealth when using items.

Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

With HeadgearWith MaskWith Helmet

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of bows, repeaters, arrows, and Stakes

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of guns, bullets, and Candy Corn

  • +51 defense
  • +13% ranged damage
  • ×1.12[1] damage of specialist ranged weapons (non-consumable ranged weapons that are not bows or guns) and their ammunition

  • +25% ranged critical strike chance
  • +20% ammo conservation
  • +12% movement speed
  • The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving
  • Standing still and not using any items causes the player to quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 1.12 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:[2]
    • +60% ranged damage
    • +10% ranged critical strike chance
    • −750 aggro
    • +50% ranged knockback

Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount[3] or taking damage[4]. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).
